description.narrative: In late 2013 in response to the Syria Crisis and protracted humanitarian situation the Lebanese Red Cross most well-known for running the national ambulance service - formed a Disaster Management Unit (DMU). Throughout 2014 and 2015 the DMU has grown from a handful of staff in HQ to an HQ team of around 20 staff and 12 branch teams of DM volunteers. However whilst the DMU has a growing programme portfolio including Relief (in-kind and cash) WASH and DRR budget and geographical reach across Lebanon the unit does not have an assistance strategy nor does it have the tools it needs to operate effectively manage risk and plan for sustainability. Through discussions with LRCS and other Movement Partners it has been identified that a coherent DM strategy is required that will clarify what the DMU will focus on where and how it is proposed that BRC s partnership with LRCS takes the form of a two-year engagement plan in order to: Support the DMU to develop an assistance strategy and associated management tools and processes. Linked to this provide support at the strategic and programme level in PMER starting with a PMER capacity self-assessment and moving on to tailored remote support as needed. PMER support will be programme specific and aligned to the National PMER capacity building initiative supported by Norwegian Red Cross. The first steps in the strategy development process will be: a) an evaluation of LRCS cash and in kind work from both a technical and a value for money perspective with a view to collecting more evidence regarding the relevance and appropriateness of cash as a response modality for LRCS; and b) a DM scoping study to better understand the DM opportunities in the region (needs what other National Societies and humanitarian actors are doing gaps etc) and what the options for growth are. The DM strategy will be developed in coordination with other key actors supporting LRCS DMU such as the German and Netherlands Red Cross and ICRC. Provide continued embedded CTP technical support in order to allow for on-going institutionalisation of the processes established during the pilot to implement findings from the recent review of the pilot and to strategically engage in CTP preparedness work across a number of DM branches (including the piloting of different CTP modalities and/or delivery mechanisms)
